newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: U.S. envoy denies insulting Colombian government.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy denies insulting Colombian government.

text.p: The U.S. Embassy in Bogota on Tuesday denied that Ambassador Myles Frechette had described Colombia's scandal-plagued government as "shit" in an interview with a prominent journalist.
Frechette has often suggested that he thought President Ernesto Samper and close aides accepted millions of dollars in drug money to support Samper's 1994 election campaign.
According to a new book, "The President Who Was Going to Fall," Frechette used the expletive to describe Samper's government in September 1995.

The book is co-authored by Mauricio Vargas, head of the prestigious weekly news magazine Semana, who said he asked Frechette about Washington's view of the Colombian government in an off-the-record interview on Sept. 30, 1995.
According to Vargas, Frechette replied: "that it's shit."

In a brief statement, the embassy said: "The statements published on page 344 of the book 'The President Who Was Going to Fall,' attributed to U.S. Ambassador to Colombia Myles R.R. Frechette on Sept. 30, 1995, are false."
